values.notes: Artificial identifier; does not encode source row or submission time. Join the two individual-response files by this column. Background has 51 consenting respondents; interests has 49; 49 consented to both.

variable.name: prog.prof
variable.description: Self-rated proficiency in programming
question.text:
How would you describe your proficiency with programming, relative to a typical undergraduate student?

Consider a 'typical' student to mean a current UCSB undergraduate from any major and any class standing.
values.notes: beg = Beginner; int = Intermediate; adv = Advanced. Relative to a typical current UCSB undergraduate from any major and class standing. Numeric scores 1, 2, 3 impose equal spacing between categories.

variable.name: prog.comf
variable.description: Self-rated comfort with programming
question.text: Regardless of your skill level, how would you describe your comfort level with programming?
values.notes: Original numeric response; observed values are 2, 3, 4, 5.

variable.name: upper_div_courses
variable.description: Approximate number of upper-division courses in statistics/probability, mathematics, or programming
question.text: All together, about how many upper-division UCSB courses (or transferrable equivalents) have you taken in at least one of the above areas (statistics and probability, mathematics, and programming)?

variable.name: courses
variable.description: Completed courses selected by the respondent
question.text:
Which of the following classes have you completed? Please check all that apply.

For a series (e.g., PSTAT 120A-B), check the box if you have taken any course in the series.

Please do not include courses in progress.
values.notes: Comma-separated course labels in one cell. A series label means at least one course in that series. Excludes courses in progress. Split into one respondent/course per row to count selections; denominator for proportions is 51 shared background respondents.

variable.name: domain_specialization
variable.description: Whether the respondent reports a domain specialization
question.text:
Would you describe yourself as having any domain specialization (e.g. biology, linguistics, environmental science, physics, etc.)?

Consider "domain specialization" to mean upper-division coursework or equivalent experience in any field.
values.notes: Yes; No; Unsure. The accompanying free-text description is excluded.

variable.name: research
variable.description: Any supervised research experience, combining data-science and other research
question.text:
Not including class projects or personal projects, do you have any experience doing supervised research activity involving data science?

Not including class projects or personal projects, do you have any experience doing supervised research activity not involving data science?
values.notes: Derived: Yes if either source response is Yes; No if both are No; Unsure otherwise. Excludes class and personal projects. Research-type distinctions and free-text descriptions are excluded.

variable.name: response_id
variable.description: Artificial respondent identifier
values.notes: Artificial identifier; does not encode source row or submission time. Join the two individual-response files by this column. Background has 51 consenting respondents; interests has 49; 49 consented to both.

variable.name: type
variable.description: Preference for an industry or research-lab project
question.text: Do you have any preference regarding working on an industry project or a research lab project?
values.notes: ind = industry; lab = research lab; both = no preference. The code both does not indicate an explicit request for both types.

variable.name: language
variable.description: Preferred programming language
question.text: Would you prefer to work with a specific programming language?
values.notes: R; Python; No preference.

variable.name: domains
variable.description: Application domains of interest
question.text: Which of the following domains are of interest to you? Check all that apply.
values.notes: Original multi-selection text, including additional interest labels. Commas separate standard options, but additional text may also contain commas; inspect before splitting.

variable.name: areas
variable.description: Areas of data science of interest
question.text: Which of the following areas of data science are of interest to you? Check all that apply.
values.notes: Original multi-selection text. Do not split naively on commas: Predictive modeling, generally and Statistical models and inference, generally each contain an internal comma. Match complete option labels instead.

variable.name: group
variable.description: Summary variable or grouping
values.notes: standing; gender; race; primary_major; second_major; consent. Aggregate summaries cover all 55 respondents and have no respondent identifiers.

variable.name: category
variable.description: Category within the summary group
values.notes: Demographic labels or consent combinations. For consent, the format is skills consent / project consent, with Yes or No for each. Obvious major spelling variants are consolidated; ambiguous majors remain distinct. The free-text gender response is labeled Another self-description; Junior (senior credits) remains separate. None reported denotes no reported second major.

variable.name: n
variable.description: Number of respondents in the category
values.notes: Counts within each group sum to 55. Do not add counts across groups as though they represented distinct respondents.

variable.name: percent
variable.description: Percentage of all survey respondents in the category
values.notes: 100 * n / 55, rounded to one decimal place; values range from 0 to 100, not 0 to 1. Rounded percentages may not sum to exactly 100.

variable.name: date
variable.description: Local calendar date of submission
values.notes: YYYY-MM-DD. Source timestamps have no timezone metadata and are assumed to be America/Los_Angeles. Includes each date from the first to last response, including zero-response dates. Individual timestamps are excluded.

variable.name: n
variable.description: Number of survey responses submitted on that date
values.notes: Daily counts cover all 55 responses. Assignment deadline: October 4, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Pacific. Original timestamps give 54 on-time and 1 late response; exact deadline classification cannot generally be reconstructed from daily counts alone.
